mainTopic: עירוב תבשילין: its rules, sources and reasons, and how to spend יום טוב
overview: The משנה teaches that when יום טוב falls on Friday, you may not cook on יום טוב with the plan of cooking for שבת, though leftovers from יום טוב cooking may be eaten on שבת. To permit this cooking, חכמים created עירוב תבשילין: a dish cooked before יום טוב that you rely on to cook for שבת. בית שמאי require two dishes and בית הלל one, and even a small leftover of the dish is enough. The גמרא gives two sources for the rule: שמואל's reading of 'זכור את יום השבת' and a תנא's reading of 'את אשר תאפו אפו'. רבא says the עירוב makes sure a good portion is saved for שבת. רב אשי says it teaches that cooking on יום טוב for another day is forbidden. A story follows about רבי אליעזר criticizing people who left his יום טוב lecture to go eat, which leads to his dispute with רבי יהושע about whether a person must split יום טוב between Torah and festive eating. The amud ends by explaining phrases of the verse in נחמיה, adding a side teaching about the אֶדֶר tree, and introducing a ברייתא taught by רב תחליפא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No cooking on יום טוב for שבת, but leftovers are fine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the basic rule: on a יום טוב that falls on Friday, you may not start cooking for שבת. You may cook for יום טוב, and whatever is left over may be eaten on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When יום טוב falls on Friday, a person may not cook on יום טוב from the start for שבת. But he may cook for יום טוב, and if food is left over, it is left over for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets the starting rule: cooking on יום טוב is allowed only for יום טוב itself, not for the next day, even when the next day is שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking is permitted on יום טוב because it is for that day's needs. Cooking for a different day, even שבת, is not covered by that permission. The key word is בתחלה, 'from the start': your intention when you cook is what matters, so leftovers from honest יום טוב cooking are fine.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, with this as your original intention

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: A Festival that falls on Shabbat eve (Friday)

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְבַשֵּׁל בַּתְּחִלָּה מִיּוֹם טוֹב לְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: one may not cook from the outset on the Festival for Shabbat.
But he may cook for the Festival,
and if he left some over, he has left it over for Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Leftovers from cooking done for יום טוב may be eaten on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a יום טוב that falls on Friday, you may not cook for שבת from the start. Cooking for יום טוב is allowed, and leftovers may be used on שבת.

steps.title: Preparing a dish before יום טוב to permit cooking for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה introduces עירוב תבשילין: you make a cooked dish on ערב יום טוב and rely on it to cook on יום טוב for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person makes a cooked dish on the day before יום טוב, and relies on it to cook for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the solution to the restriction in step 1. Preparing a dish before יום טוב allows you to cook for שבת on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dish is prepared before יום טוב starts, on a regular weekday. Because the שבת preparations have already 'begun' before יום טוב, the cooking you do on יום טוב for שבת is treated as continuing them. This is a rabbinic arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'joining of cooked foods,' the name of this arrangement

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse עירוב תבשילין with עירוב חצרות or עירוב תחומין. Those deal with carrying and walking limits. This עירוב is only about cooking on יום טוב for שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the practice, still done today, of setting aside bread and a cooked food such as an egg before a Friday יום טוב.

phrases.english: And one prepares a cooked dish on the Festival eve,
and relies on it to cook for Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the solution that permits the cooking forbidden in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dish cooked before יום טוב allows you to cook on יום טוב for שבת.

steps.title: How many dishes are needed: one or two
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי require two cooked dishes for the עירוב, and בית הלל require only one. Both agree that a fish with an egg on it counts as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say two dishes are needed. בית הלל say one dish is enough. Both agree that a fish with an egg cooked on it counts as two dishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a disagreement about the details of עירוב תבשילין: how many cooked items are required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי are stricter and want two dishes. בית הלל say one is enough, and the הלכה generally follows בית הלל. Their point of agreement shows that two different foods cooked together, a fish and the egg on it, still count as two dishes.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: two cooked dishes,
and Beit Hillel say: one cooked dish.
And they agree regarding a fish and the egg that is on it,
that they count as two cooked dishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the details of the עירוב introduced in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי require two dishes and בית הלל require one. A fish with an egg on it counts as two according to both.

steps.title: If the dish is eaten or lost
steps.stepSummary: If the עירוב dish was eaten or lost, you may no longer cook for שבת based on it. If any amount at all remains, you may still rely on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate it or it was lost, he may not start cooking based on it. If he left over any amount of it, he may rely on it for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by explaining that the עירוב dish must still exist when you do the cooking for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עירוב works only while the dish is still around. Once it is gone, the permission to cook for שבת ends. Even a tiny leftover (כל שהוא) keeps the permission alive.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rules: (1) no cooking on יום טוב for שבת from the start, though leftovers are fine; (2) an עירוב תבשילין made before יום טוב permits it; (3) בית הלל require one dish; (4) the dish, or some part of it, must still exist.

phrases.english: If he ate it or it was lost,
he may not cook from the outset relying on it.
But if he left over any amount of it,
he may rely on it for Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition on the עירוב: it must still exist when you cook.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An eaten or lost עירוב no longer permits cooking for שבת. Any remaining amount does.

steps.title: Where does this rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rules about cooking on יום טוב for שבת and עירוב תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the משנה's law. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנא הני מילי is the standard question asking for a source. Here it asks where the restriction on cooking for שבת, and the עירוב that permits it, come from.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
From where are these words (derived)? A request for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the entire משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rules of עירוב תבשילין and for not cooking on יום טוב for שבת without it.

steps.title: שמואל: remember שבת so another day does not make you forget it
steps.stepSummary: שמואל cites 'זכור את יום השבת לקדשו' and explains: remember שבת so that another holy day does not make you forget it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The פסוק says, 'Remember the שבת day to keep it holy.' Remember it, so that another day that comes along does not make you forget it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by connecting the עירוב to the פסוק of זכור. When יום טוב comes right before שבת, people could get so busy with יום טוב that they neglect שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads 'זכור' as a warning to keep שבת in mind even when יום טוב comes first. The עירוב makes a person think about שבת before יום טוב even begins, so שבת is not forgotten. The פסוק serves as support for a rabbinic enactment.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the Torah itself commands עירוב תבשילין. The עירוב is a rabbinic institution, and the פסוק explains the concern behind it: that שבת not be forgotten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the purpose of the עירוב: to protect the honor and memory of שבת when יום טוב falls right before it.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, עירוב תבשילין exists so that שבת is remembered and not pushed aside by a יום טוב that comes right before it.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
As the verse states:
"Remember the Shabbat day to keep it holy" (Exodus 20:8),
remember it, against another day that comes to make it forgotten.
phrases.notes: The 'other day' is the יום טוב that falls on Friday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'זכור את יום השבת לקדשו': remember שבת so that the יום טוב before it does not make you forget it.

steps.title: What is the reason behind the enactment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the deeper reason why חכמים created עירוב תבשילין to protect שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why חכמים chose this enactment to keep people from forgetting שבת. This short question sets up two different answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל told us that the עירוב is a reminder about שבת. He did not say how it helps or what could go wrong without it. The גמרא wants that concern spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked dish prepared before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: What exactly is the concern that the עירוב addresses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind שמואל's explanation that the עירוב prevents forgetting שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific concern that led חכמים to institute עירוב תבשילין.

steps.title: רבא: so that a good portion is saved for שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the עירוב makes a person set aside a choice portion for שבת as well as for יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: So that a person will choose a nice portion for שבת and a nice portion for יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the first answer. The עירוב makes sure a person thinks about שבת and saves good food for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יום טוב comes right before שבת, a person might use up all the best food on יום טוב. By preparing something for שבת ahead of time, he is reminded to honor שבת too. For רבא, the עירוב is about showing respect for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A choice, nice portion of food

phrases.english: Rava said:
So that he will select a nice portion for Shabbat
and a nice portion for the Festival.
phrases.notes: Both days get honored. שבת is not swallowed up by יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עירוב ensures that a choice portion is set aside for שבת, so שבת is honored.

steps.title: רב אשי: so people know baking on יום טוב for another day is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the עירוב teaches people that cooking on יום טוב for שבת is normally forbidden, and certainly cooking for a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: So that people will say, 'One may not bake on יום טוב for שבת.' Then they will reason with a קל וחומר: certainly one may not bake on יום טוב for a regular weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer. The עירוב is a visible sign that cooking on יום טוב for a later day is not normally allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, the concern is protecting יום טוב, not honoring שבת. People see that even cooking for שבת needs a special עירוב, so they learn that cooking for another day is normally forbidden. From that they conclude with a קל וחומר that cooking on יום טוב for a weekday is certainly forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (an argument from a lighter case to a stronger one)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא and רב אשי both agree that the עירוב exists. They disagree about who it protects. רבא says it protects the honor of שבת. רב אשי says it protects יום טוב from being used to cook for other days.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
So that people will say:
One may not bake on a Festival for Shabbat,
and all the more so from a Festival for a weekday.
phrases.notes: If even שבת needs an עירוב, cooking for a weekday is certainly forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עירוב reminds people that cooking on יום טוב for another day is forbidden without it.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא: why must the עירוב be made before יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the עירוב is made on ערב יום טוב. That fits רב אשי, but according to רבא it could be made on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: A person makes a cooked dish on ערב יום טוב and relies on it for שבת. This works well for רב אשי, who says the point is that people will learn one may not bake on יום טוב for שבת. That is why it is made on ערב יום טוב and not on יום טוב. But according to רבא, why does it have to be on ערב יום טוב? Even on יום טוב itself it should work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה to test both opinions. The wording fits רב אשי well, but it seems to cause a problem for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, making the עירוב on יום טוב itself would undo the whole lesson, since the point is that cooking on יום טוב for שבת is not allowed. For רבא, the goal is only to set aside a good portion for שבת, and that could be done on יום טוב too. So why does the משנה insist on ערב יום טוב?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (according to one opinion), before a 'but' (אלא)

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna:
One makes a cooked dish on the Festival eve
and relies on it for Shabbat.
It makes sense according to Rav Ashi,
phrases.notes: Setup: first the גמרא shows which opinion fits easily.

phrases.english: who said: so that people will say
one may not bake on a Festival for Shabbat,
that is why on the Festival eve, yes,
but on the Festival itself, no.
But according to Rava,
phrases.notes: Now comes the difficulty.

phrases.english: why specifically on the Festival eve?
Even on the Festival as well!
phrases.notes: Saving a good portion for שבת could be done on יום טוב itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two reasons from steps 8 and 9 against the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that the עירוב is meant to save a choice portion for שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires the עירוב on ערב יום טוב. רבא's goal could be met on יום טוב itself, so the requirement seems pointless according to him.

steps.title: Answer: a decree in case he neglects to do it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that by רבא's logic it could be done on יום טוב. חכמים still required it beforehand in case a person would neglect it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But חכמים made a גזירה, in case the person neglects it and never makes it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It admits his reason alone would allow making the עירוב on יום טוב, but adds a practical safeguard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a busy יום טוב, a person might push off preparing for שבת and end up never doing it. To prevent that, חכמים required the עירוב on ערב יום טוב. רבא's reason stays, and the timing comes from an extra גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

steps.whatToRemember: רבא says the עירוב honors שבת by saving a good portion for it. רב אשי says it teaches that cooking on יום טוב for another day is forbidden. רבא still requires it on ערב יום טוב because of a גזירה, in case a person neglects it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the עירוב must be prepared before יום טוב even according to רבא. The answer uses a classic pattern: the basic logic would allow more, but חכמים added a safeguard.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
phrases.notes: The גמרא concedes the point of the question.

phrases.english: but it is a decree, lest he be negligent.
phrases.notes: He might keep delaying and never prepare for שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יִפְשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and defends רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession plus a rabbinic decree (אין הכי נמי, אלא גזירה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבא, the עירוב could be made on יום טוב itself, so the משנה's ערב יום טוב requirement seems pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא agrees in principle, but חכמים required ערב יום טוב as a safeguard in case a person neglects to prepare it.

steps.title: A second verse as the source for the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: A תנא brings the verse about baking and cooking for the first שבת, and רבי אליעזר learns from it that new cooking must rely on food already prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא brings the source from this verse: "Bake what you will bake, and cook what you will cook." From here רבי אליעזר said: one may bake only on top of what is already baked, and cook only on top of what is already cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different verse as the source for עירוב תבשילין. It then shows how רבי אליעזר reads that verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse comes from the day before the first שבת in the desert, when the people prepared the מן for שבת ahead of time. רבי אליעזר reads it as saying that cooking for שבת should be added on to food that was already made. That is exactly what the עירוב does: food is cooked on ערב יום טוב, and the cooking on יום טוב for שבת builds on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of the era of the משנה and ברייתא
He brings it (the source) from here

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר means the Torah itself requires an עירוב תבשילין. The next line says חכמים only 'leaned on' this verse as a hint (סמכו).

phrases.english: And a tanna brings it from here:
phrases.notes: A second source, alongside the one quoted earlier in the sugya.

phrases.english: "That which you will bake, bake
phrases.notes: Exodus 16:23, said on the day before the first שבת.

phrases.english: and that which you will cook, cook"
From here Rabbi Eliezer said:
One may bake only on that which is already baked,
phrases.notes: New baking for שבת relies on bread prepared beforehand.

phrases.english: and one may cook only on that which is already cooked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבא and רב אשי discussion ends, the גמרא gives another source for עירוב תבשילין.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of עירוב תבשילין: cooking on יום טוב for שבת by relying on food prepared before יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Exodus 16:23, 'את אשר תאפו אפו ואת אשר תבשלו בשלו', as read by רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: חכמים based the עירוב on this verse as a hint
steps.stepSummary: From this verse, חכמים found Torah support for their enactment of עירוב תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here חכמים found support in the Torah for עירוב תבשילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the source section. The verse is the Torah hint that חכמים relied on for the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סמכו ('they leaned on') shows the עירוב is a rabbinic enactment. The verse is a support for it, not a strict Torah command. This ties the earlier reasons from רבא and רב אשי to a Torah pattern of preparing for שבת ahead of time.

keyTerms.meaning: They leaned on (found support in a verse for a rabbinic law)
Joining of cooked foods, which allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת
From the Torah (here meaning a hint, not a command)

steps.whatToRemember: עירוב תבשילין is a rabbinic enactment. Its Torah hint is 'את אשר תאפו אפו': prepare for שבת ahead of time, and build on what is already made.

phrases.english: From here the Sages leaned (found support)
for the joining of cooked foods, from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from רבי אליעזר's reading of the verse in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The verse 'את אשר תאפו אפו' is the Torah hint (אסמכתא) for the rabbinic enactment of עירוב תבשילין.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's all-day lecture and the first groups who leave
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבי אליעזר taught the laws of יום טוב all day. As groups left early, he described each one by the size of its wine container.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: once רבי אליעזר sat and taught the laws of יום טוב the whole day. The first group left, and he said: these are owners of huge vats. A second group left, and he said: these are owners of barrels. A third group left, and he said: these are owners of jugs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about רבי אליעזר, who was mentioned in the last steps. People leave his יום טוב lecture to go home and eat, and he comments on each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group that leaves is described by a smaller wine container than the one before. The idea is that the people with the biggest feasts waiting for them left first. His words are a sharp criticism of people who leave Torah learning for food.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: There was an incident with Rabbi Eliezer
who was sitting and lecturing

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ בְּהִלְכוֹת יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: the entire day about the laws of the Festival.
The first group left,
he said: These are owners of huge vats.
phrases.notes: They have big feasts waiting at home.

phrases.aramaic: כַּת שְׁנִיָּה, אָמַר: הַלָּלוּ בַּעֲלֵי חָבִיּוֹת.
phrases.english: A second group; he said: These are owners of barrels.

phrases.aramaic: כַּת שְׁלִישִׁית, אָמַר: הַלָּלוּ בַּעֲלֵי כַדִּין.
phrases.english: A third group; he said: These are owners of jugs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי אליעזר was just quoted, the גמרא brings a story about him and his attitude toward eating on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר criticized those who left his יום טוב lecture to go eat, describing them by their wine containers.

steps.title: More groups leave, and the sixth group is called cursed
steps.stepSummary: Groups four and five are described by even smaller containers. When the sixth group starts to leave, רבי אליעזר calls them 'owners of a curse'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A fourth group left, and he said: these are owners of jars. A fifth group left, and he said: these are owners of cups. When a sixth group began to leave, he said: these are owners of a curse.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues as more groups leave. רבי אליעזר's comments grow sharper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The containers keep shrinking, from jars down to cups. The sixth group has no feast waiting at all, yet they still leave. So he calls them 'owners of a curse', since they gave up Torah for nothing.

phrases.aramaic: כַּת רְבִיעִית, אָמַר: הַלָּלוּ בַּעֲלֵי לְגִינִין.
phrases.english: A fourth group; he said: These are owners of jars.

phrases.aramaic: כַּת חֲמִישִׁית, אָמַר: הַלָּלוּ בַּעֲלֵי כוֹסוֹת.
phrases.english: A fifth group; he said: These are owners of cups.
A sixth group began to leave,
he said: These are owners of a curse.
phrases.notes: They leave though nothing is waiting for them, and the study hall is left almost empty.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּת רְבִיעִית, אָמַר: הַלָּלוּ בַּעֲלֵי לְגִינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the groups leaving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The groups who left were described by ever-smaller containers, and the last were called 'owners of a curse'.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר reassures the students who stayed
steps.stepSummary: The remaining students grew pale, thinking he meant them. He explained that he meant only those who left eternal life for passing life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He looked at the students, and their faces began to change color. He said to them: my sons, I am not talking about you. I am talking about those who left, because they leave eternal life and busy themselves with temporary life.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי אליעזר explaining who his harsh words were for and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students who stayed were afraid his words were aimed at them. He makes clear that those who stayed did the right thing. The criticism is for those who chose a temporary meal (חיי שעה) over eternal Torah (חיי עולם).

keyTerms.meaning: He cast his eyes, looked at
Changing (their faces changed color out of fear or shame)
Temporary life, meaning physical needs like eating

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's lesson: leaving Torah learning just to rush to a meal means trading חיי עולם for חיי שעה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows how רבי אליעזר valued spending יום טוב in Torah learning over feasting. This sets up the גמרא's coming discussion of how a person should divide the day of יום טוב.

phrases.english: He cast his eyes upon the students,
their faces began to change color.
phrases.notes: They feared he meant them.

phrases.english: He said to them: My sons,
I am not speaking about you,
but about those who left,
who abandon eternal life
and engage in temporary life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by explaining the point of רבי אליעזר's sharp remarks, before his parting words in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Those who left Torah learning on יום טוב for food were criticized for choosing חיי שעה over חיי עולם. Those who stayed were praised.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר sends off the remaining students with a blessing
steps.stepSummary: When the students who stayed until the end finally left, רבי אליעזר quoted a verse from נחמיה telling them to go eat, drink, and rejoice.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they left, he told them: "Go, eat rich food and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to people who have nothing ready. The day is holy to our Lord. Do not be sad, because the joy of ה׳ is your strength."
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the ברייתא's story. רבי אליעזר blesses the students who stayed to the end and sends them home to enjoy their festive meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students who left early were criticized, but the ones who stayed for the full day of learning are now told to go eat and celebrate. This shows that רבי אליעזר was not against eating on יום טוב. He only objected to leaving Torah in the middle of learning in order to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: portions of food sent as gifts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר opposed festive meals. The same students he praised are sent off to eat. His complaint was about people who walked out of Torah learning early.

phrases.english: At the time of their departure, he said to them:
"Go, eat rich foods
and drink sweet drinks
and send portions to whoever has nothing prepared
phrases.notes: נחמיה ח:י

phrases.english: for the day is holy to our Lord
and do not be sad
for the joy of ה׳ is your strength."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא story begun in steps 14-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who learned the whole day are sent off to rejoice with food and drink.

steps.title: But festive joy is itself a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's words from step 16. How can eating on יום טוב be called 'temporary life' when שמחת יום טוב is a מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said that they leave eternal life and busy themselves with temporary life. But the joy of יום טוב is a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's explanation and attacks it. Rejoicing on יום טוב is a מצוה, so leaving to eat should not count as chasing 'temporary life.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treated the festive meal as worldly and short-lived. But if eating on יום טוב fulfills a מצוה, then those students were also doing something spiritual. So his criticism seems unfair.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', a formula for quoting an earlier statement in order to analyze it
the obligation to rejoice on a festival

phrases.english: The Master said:
that they leave eternal life
and busy themselves with temporary life

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא שִׂמְחַת יוֹם טוֹב מִצְוָה הִיא!
phrases.english: But the joy of Yom Tov is a מצוה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא שִׂמְחַת יוֹם טוֹב מִצְוָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation רבי אליעזר gave in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's description of festive eating as 'חיי שעה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Festive joy is a מצוה, so engaging in it cannot be dismissed as merely worldly.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר holds festive joy is optional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר is consistent with his own view, which is that שמחת יום טוב is only רשות (optional).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning, because he said that the joy of יום טוב is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. According to רבי אליעזר, eating for joy on יום טוב is not a required מצוה, so calling it 'temporary life' makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that everyone agrees festive joy is a מצוה. The answer shows that רבי אליעזר disagrees. For him festive eating is only permitted and good, not required, so leaving Torah for it is a real loss.

keyTerms.meaning: follows his own reasoning, consistent with his view elsewhere

steps.confusionAlert: רשות here does not mean eating is bad or forbidden. It means it is optional rather than an obligation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning,
for he said: the joy of Yom Tov is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the assumption: the premise of the challenge is not accepted by רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Festive joy is a מצוה for everyone, so eating is also 'eternal life'.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר festive joy is רשות, so leaving Torah for it is leaving eternal life for temporary life.

steps.title: Proof: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע on how to spend יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר's view. On יום טוב a person either eats and drinks or sits and learns. רבי יהושע says to split the day half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says a person on יום טוב does either of two things: he eats and drinks, or he sits and learns. רבי יהושע says: divide it, half for ה׳ and half for yourselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי אליעזר treats festive joy as optional. He allows a person to spend the whole day learning without eating festively.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person may choose to learn all day, then eating for joy cannot be required, so it is רשות. רבי יהושע disagrees and requires both parts every יום טוב. That means for him festive joy is a real requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
half for ה׳ and half for you

steps.whyThisMatters: The הלכה generally follows רבי יהושע's balanced model: part of יום טוב for Torah and תפילה, and part for festive eating.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A person has nothing on Yom Tov
except either eating and drinking,
or sitting and learning.
Rabbi Yehoshua says: divide it:
half for ה׳, and half for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 19 that רבי אליעזר holds שמחת יום טוב is רשות.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר holds festive joy is optional.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר allows either all eating or all learning, against רבי יהושע's half-and-half.

steps.title: Both opinions come from the same two verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that both תנאים learned their views from the same pair of verses. One verse says the festival is 'for ה׳ your God' and the other says it is 'for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from the same verse. One verse says, "an assembly for ה׳ your God," and another verse says, "an assembly shall be for you." How do these fit together?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן points out two verses that seem to contradict each other. He asks how they fit together, which sets up the next step where each תנא gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse makes the festival sound fully devoted to ה׳, and the other makes it sound like a celebration for the people. Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע have to explain both verses. Their argument is about how to resolve this tension.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How do the verses fit together?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And both of them expounded one verse.
One verse says:
"An assembly for ה׳ your God"
phrases.notes: דברים טז:ח

phrases.english: and one verse says:
"It shall be an assembly for you."
phrases.notes: במדבר כט:לה

phrases.english: How so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural root of the dispute brought in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both תנאים resolve the same apparent contradiction between 'for ה׳' and 'for you'.

steps.title: Each opinion resolves the verses differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the verses as a choice: the day goes all to ה׳ or all to you. רבי יהושע reads them as a combination: half to ה׳ and half to you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: either the whole day for ה׳, or the whole day for you. רבי יהושע holds: divide it, half for ה׳ and half for you.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the 'how so' question. Each תנא explains how both verses can be true at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats the two verses as two possible options, and you may choose either one. רבי יהושע says you must fulfill both verses every יום טוב, so the day is split. This is why festive joy is optional for רבי אליעזר and required for רבי יהושע.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: יום טוב is all Torah or all eating, a choice, so festive joy is רשות. רבי יהושע: half for ה׳ and half for you, so both parts are required. Both opinions come from the verses 'עצרת לה׳ אלהיך' and 'עצרת תהיה לכם'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לַה׳, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לָכֶם.
phrases.english: either all of it for ה׳, or all of it for you.
And Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
divide it, half for ה׳ and half for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לַה׳, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'הא כיצד' question posed in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the two verses are reconciled.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר: either/or. רבי יהושע: split the day.

steps.title: What does 'to him for whom nothing is prepared' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of a phrase from the verse in נחמיה that was quoted earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'to him for whom nothing is prepared'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the verse in נחמיה that the ברייתא quoted and asks what one phrase means. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse tells people to send food portions to someone 'who has nothing prepared.' The verse does not say who this person is or why he lacks food on a holy day. The גמרא wants to identify him.

keyTerms.meaning: To one who has nothing prepared (נחמיה 8:10)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. The argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is finished. The גמרא is now explaining phrases from the verse in נחמיה.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'to him for whom nothing is prepared'?
phrases.notes: From נחמיה 8:10, which was quoted earlier in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע discussion to explain a verse quoted earlier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the person in the verse who 'has nothing prepared'?

steps.title: רב חסדא: someone who did not make an עירובי תבשילין
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the verse means a person who did not set up עירובי תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It means someone who did not set aside an עירובי תבשילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The person with 'nothing prepared' is someone who did not make an עירובי תבשילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב falls on Friday, a person may cook on יום טוב for שבת only if he set up an עירובי תבשילין beforehand. Without it, he cannot cook for שבת, so he truly has 'nothing prepared.' Others should send him food.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
To one who did not set aside an eruv tavshilin.
phrases.notes: So he cannot cook on יום טוב for שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person with 'nothing prepared' is someone without an עירובי תבשילין.

steps.title: Second version: only someone who could not make one
steps.stepSummary: A second version of רב חסדא's words limits the verse to someone who had no chance to make an עירובי תבשילין. Someone who could have made one and did not is negligent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he said: It means someone who was not able to set aside an עירובי תבשילין. But someone who was able to set one aside and did not is negligent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב חסדא's answer. It narrows down who deserves to be sent food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, anyone without an עירוב is included. In this version, only someone who had no opportunity to make one (מי שלא היה לו להניח) is included. Someone who had the chance and did not make one is called a פושע (negligent), and the verse does not require us to help him.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (introduces a second version of a statement)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that argues with רב חסדא. It is a second report of what רב חסדא himself said.

phrases.english: Some say:
One who did not have the opportunity
to set aside an eruv tavshilin,
but one who had the opportunity
to set aside an eruv tavshilin
and did not set it aside — he is negligent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a narrower second version of רב חסדא's answer in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only someone who could not make an עירוב counts. A negligent person is not included.

steps.title: What does 'the joy of ה׳ is your strength' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the meaning of the end of the same verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'for the joy of ה׳ is your strength'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another phrase from the same verse in נחמיה. This line sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear how the 'joy of ה׳' becomes a person's 'strength' or support. The גמרא wants to know what this phrase is teaching.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'for the joy of the Lord is your strength'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question about the same verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'the joy of ה׳ is your strength' teach?

steps.title: Borrow on My account and I will repay
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון, explains that ה׳ tells the Jews to borrow money to honor the holy day and promises to repay them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to the Jewish people: My children, borrow on My account, and make קידוש for the holiness of the day. Trust in Me, and I will pay it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. ה׳ promises to repay whatever a person borrows to celebrate שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'joy of ה׳' is the celebration of His holy days, and this joy is your 'strength' because ה׳ Himself guarantees the cost. So a person should not hold back from honoring the day just because he lacks money.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of the day (honored with קידוש over wine)

steps.whatToRemember: Spending to honor שבת and יום טוב is backed by ה׳'s promise: 'Borrow on My account, and I will repay.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
My children, borrow on My account,
and sanctify the holiness of the day,
phrases.notes: Make קידוש with wine.

phrases.english: and trust in Me, and I will repay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ guarantees repayment of money borrowed to honor the holy day.

steps.title: Plant an אֶדֶר tree to protect your property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another teaching of the same teacher: planting an אֶדֶר tree keeps one's property safe, based on the word אַדִּיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון: Whoever wants his property to last should plant an אֶדֶר tree in it, as the verse says: 'ה׳ on high is mighty (אַדִּיר).'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted this teacher, it adds another of his teachings on a new subject: the אֶדֶר tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is based on how the words sound. אֶדֶר sounds like אַדִּיר (mighty), and ה׳ is called אַדִּיר. So the tree carries a sign of strength and lasting power.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of tree (some say a type of cedar)

steps.confusionAlert: This teaching is not related to יום טוב. It is included only because it comes from the same chain of teachers (רבי יוחנן quoting רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon:
One who wants his property to endure —
should plant an eder tree among it,
as it is said: 'The Lord on high is mighty (adir).'
phrases.notes: תהלים 93:4. The proof is that אֶדֶר and אַדִּיר sound alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching added because it has the same chain of teachers as step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planting an אֶדֶר tree helps one's property last, based on the word אַדִּיר.

steps.title: Another reason: the name means 'lasting for generations'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second explanation: the name אַדְרָא itself hints that it lasts for generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, alternatively, the אַדְרָא is like its name. As people say: Why is it called אַדְרָא? Because it lasts for generations upon generations (דָּרֵי דָּרֵי).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different source for the same idea. This time the source is a popular saying about the tree's name, not a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of linking אֶדֶר to אַדִּיר, this explanation links אַדְרָא to דָּרֵי (generations). The tree lives a very long time, so the property it is planted in stays protected.

phrases.english: Alternatively, the eder is like its name,
as people say:
What is 'adra'?
That it endures for generations upon generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation for the teaching in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name אַדְרָא hints at its long life (דָּרֵי דָּרֵי).

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the אֶדֶר's protection
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that a field with an אֶדֶר tree is protected from theft and its fruit stays safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: A field that has an אֶדֶר tree in it is not stolen and not seized by force, and its fruit is kept safe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the idea that the אֶדֶר tree protects property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives practical results. Because the tree is a clear sign of who owns the field, no one can steal the field or take it by force. Its fruit is also preserved, because the tree protects it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא brought as support)
Taken by force (often with some payment)

steps.whatToRemember: An אֶדֶר tree protects property. Two reasons are given: the word אַדִּיר, and the name meaning 'lasting for generations.' A ברייתא supports this.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
A field that has an eder tree in it
is not stolen and is not seized by force,
and its fruits are preserved.

steps.title: Introducing a teaching taught by רב תחליפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא recited by רב תחליפא, the brother of רבנאי חוזאה, as it returns to the topic of spending for the holy days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא, the brother of רבנאי from חוזאה, taught a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא names who taught the next teaching, and the teaching itself comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תני tells us that a ברייתא is about to be quoted, not a personal opinion of an אמורא. This line also signals a return to the main topic, honoring יום טוב with money, after the side-teaching about the אדר tree in steps 28-30.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught / recited: shows a ברייתא (a teaching from the תנאים) is about to be quoted
An אמורא who recites this ברייתא
רבנאי from חוזאה (the region of בי חוזאי), mentioned to identify which רב תחליפא is meant

steps.confusionAlert: This line has no teaching of its own. Do not look for a הלכה here. It only introduces the ברייתא that comes next.
